protocolStatus: Structured research notes outside the browser-first negotiation schema; not an ABU-11/17 receipt
inputs: Parent-supplied engineering feasibility and authorization facts
productPriority: P0: one credible, polished payable workflow proving that an accepted credit invalidates prior authorization and only the freshly approved amount settles once.
rationale: The UX proposal centers the actual accounting question and makes the credit and reapproval consequence inspectable. The scope is small enough to preserve both UI quality and the authorization invariant. Engineering must confirm enforceable boundaries and evidence before final product acceptance.

detailViews: Overview with document and approval rail
Evidence tab connected to the same payable
demoControls: Test previous approval using captured old instruction
acceptedProductScope.coreSequence: 1,000 approved by A+B → accepted 200 credit → old approvals expire → previous 1,000 instruction rejected with no transfer → A+B approve 800 → 800 settles once with evidence
acceptedProductScope.visualDirection: Provisionally accept calm document-centered finance workbench with ink/paper palette, disciplined typography and restrained accent; UX to establish concrete references and tokens before implementation.

assetDecision.selected: Custom devnet Test USD mint for the fixed 1,000 / 200 / 800 scenario
assetDecision.rationale: Given the reported official devnet USDC faucet restriction, a custom test mint preserves the arithmetic and real test-network transaction proof within scope and budget.
constraints: Every transactional amount, confirmation and receipt must use Test USD consistently, not USDC or test USDC.
Persistent label: Solana devnet · Test USD · No real value.
Product context may explain that Kontor is intended for teams paying overseas contractors in USDC, immediately distinguishing this prototype's custom demonstration token.
Evidence must expose actual mint and devnet transaction identity; never imply Circle issuance, redeemability, production support or equivalent security validation.
Acceptance requires actual devnet settlement if on-chain settlement is claimed. Simulation must remain labeled and does not satisfy that claim.

implementationConstraints: Authoritative enforcement must bind approval to current payable revision, amount, mint and recipient, require two distinct approver identities, reject stale instructions and prevent duplicate settlement.
Credit acceptance and invalidation must be atomic; repeated acceptance must not double-apply the credit.
Show expired approval history separately from current approval readiness and retain blocked attempt evidence.
Pending, confirmed, failed and unknown payment outcomes must be distinct; an unknown result cannot safely create a new transfer.
No production separation-of-duties claim from synthetic persona switching.
No fake notifications, unsupported dashboard figures, invented explorer links, recall affordance or claims of traction.
UI is P0: correct amount and next action above the fold at desktop, accessible controls and statuses, readable narrow-screen stacking, persistent recoverable feedback.
Additional expenses must remain at or below $10; parent is sole control-plane writer and owns spend reconciliation.

Native Codex builders with canonical HackFleet tasks and remote compile/check gates are acceptable given missing hosted-coding credentials. Report that runtime accurately and do not call it hosted HackFleet coding-worker execution.

At most two improvement cycles. User-authorized fresh-context accountant review with non-isolated tools may proceed, but report it as a limited non-isolated review rather than genuinely blind evaluation.

rejectedAlternatives.alternative: Official devnet USDC for the fixed 1,000 scenario
rejectedAlternatives.reason: Reported faucet amount/time constraints conflict with the demo and bounded execution; revisit only if engineering has an already-authorized practical supply.

rejectedAlternatives.alternative: Scale fixed scenario down to fit official faucet
rejectedAlternatives.reason: Preserves token branding but weakens the frozen narrative; clear custom test-asset disclosure is preferable.

rejectedAlternatives.alternative: Call custom mint USDC or Test USDC
rejectedAlternatives.reason: Would misrepresent the asset and evidence.

rejectedAlternatives.alternative: Broad dashboard, integrations, customer management or fake activity
rejectedAlternatives.reason: Dilutes the central workflow and consumes the UI-quality budget.

rejectedAlternatives.alternative: Hidden stale-payment test or ordinary Pay 1,000 action after credit
rejectedAlternatives.reason: The former makes the proof undiscoverable; the latter teaches unsafe workflow. Use explicit demo control.
Does not establish user comprehension or meaningful accountant interaction.

acceptance: A fresh accountant reviewer can explain original 1,000, accepted credit 200 and amount due 800 from the normal interface.
A single identity or repeated approval by that identity cannot authorize payment.
Credit acceptance immediately invalidates the two old approvals and leaves the updated payable awaiting two new approvals.
Captured old instruction fails with no transfer and persistent understandable evidence.
Fresh distinct approvals permit exactly 800 Test USD to the intended recipient; repeated submit and refresh resolve to one settlement identity.
UI and network evidence agree on amount, mint, recipient and outcome; devnet and no-real-value labeling remain visible.
Source-aware integration checks verify invariants independently of the accountant usability review.
engineeringResponseRequired: Confirm on-chain versus server enforcement boundary and how stale revision, signer uniqueness and duplicate settlement are enforced.
Confirm devnet program deployment, minting and settlement are feasible under the budget and available execution runtime.
Provide dependency-aware task split preserving dedicated UI work, authoritative validation, automated invariant tests and end-to-end evidence.
Identify any unresolved blocker before final acceptance; simulation alone is not an undisclosed substitute for requested real test-network proof.
